questions.prompt: For \(T:\mathbb R^2 \to \mathbb R^2\) defined by \(T(x,y)=(x,0)\), find \(\ker(T)\).
questions.answer: The kernel is the set of inputs sent to zero. Solve \(T(x,y)=(0,0)\). This gives \((x,0)=(0,0)\), so \(x=0\) while y is free. Therefore \(\ker(T)=\{(0,t):t\in\mathbb R\}=\operatorname{span}((0,1))\).

questions.prompt: For \(T:\mathbb R^2 \to \mathbb R^2\) defined by \(T(x,y)=(x,0)\), find \(\operatorname{im}(T)\).
questions.answer: The image is the set of outputs \(T(x,y)\). Since \(T(x,y)=(x,0)\), every output lies on the x-axis. Every vector \((a,0)\) occurs by taking \(x=a\). Therefore \(\operatorname{im}(T)=\{(a,0):a\in\mathbb R\}=\operatorname{span}((1,0))\).

Solve \(Ax=0\). The equations are \(x+2y=0\) and \(2x+4y=0\). The second equation is twice the first, so use \(x=-2y\). Let \(y=t\). Then \(x=-2t\). Therefore \(\ker(T)=\{(-2t,t):t\in\mathbb R\}=\operatorname{span}((-2,1))\).

The image of a matrix map is the span of the columns of A. The columns are \((1,2)\) and \((2,4)\). Since \((2,4)=2(1,2)\), the column span is \(\operatorname{span}((1,2))\). Therefore \(\operatorname{im}(T)=\operatorname{span}((1,2))\).
The kernel consists of polynomials whose derivative is zero. These are exactly the constant polynomials. Therefore \(\ker(D)=\operatorname{span}(1)\).
Every polynomial in \(P_1\) has form \(a+bx\). It is the derivative of \(ax+\frac b2x^2\), which lies in \(P_2\). Therefore every element of \(P_1\) is hit by \(D\), so \(\operatorname{im}(D)=P_1\).

questions.prompt: For \(T:\mathbb R^3 \to \mathbb R\) defined by \(T(x,y,z)=x+y+z\), find \(\ker(T)\).
questions.answer: The kernel is all \((x,y,z)\) such that \(x+y+z=0\). Solve \(x=-y-z\). Let \(y=s\) and \(z=t\). Then \((x,y,z)=(-s-t,s,t)=s(-1,1,0)+t(-1,0,1)\). Therefore \(\ker(T)=\operatorname{span}((-1,1,0),(-1,0,1))\).

questions.prompt: For \(T:\mathbb R^3 \to \mathbb R\) defined by \(T(x,y,z)=x+y+z\), find \(\operatorname{im}(T)\).
questions.answer: The outputs are real numbers of the form \(x+y+z\). Every real number r can be produced by taking \((x,y,z)=(r,0,0)\). Therefore \(\operatorname{im}(T)=\mathbb R\).

questions.prompt: If \(\ker(T)=\{0\}\), what does this say about a linear map T?
questions.answer: For a linear map, \(\ker(T)=\{0\}\) means only the zero vector is sent to zero. This is equivalent to \(T\) being one-to-one. Therefore \(T\) is injective.

questions.prompt: A learner says the kernel is the set of all outputs of a linear map. Diagnose the error.
questions.answer: The set of all outputs is the image, not the kernel. The kernel is the set of inputs that are sent to the zero vector. For example, for \(T(x,y)\) = \((x,0)\), the image is the x-axis, while the kernel is the y-axis. The learner confused input-side and output-side sets.
